newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: German transport minister seeks Laarbruch talks.
newsitem.headline: German transport minister seeks Laarbruch talks.

text.p: Germany's minister of transport, Matthias Wissmann, is seeking talks with the Dutch government regarding the future of Laarbruch - a British airforce base on the German/Dutch border.
Wissmann would like to see the base turned into a civilian airport, he said in a statement.

A study, "Airport Niederrhein", has already been undertaken by the local regional council. The German initiative would like to see the air base turned into an "industrial airport" which would create an airfreight hub, where logistics companies and manufacturers would also be based.
The British airforce are due to leave the 650 hectare air base by the end of 1999.

Wissmann said Laarbruch has great potential and significant economic importance and he hoped the Dutch would support the project because of the boost it would give to the regional economies in Germany and the Netherlands.

The Dutch ministry of transport has expressed concerns about noise levels generated by any civilian development. But Wissmann said the first steps in lessening the noise had been taken as take-off and landing routes to the airport were being redesigned in a bid to lessen the noise impact.
In the Netherlands, there were also concerns that the development would bring a serious safety risk to jets deployed at a neighbouring airfield where the Dutch Royal Airforce has a base.
Wissmann's statement said he hoped to discuss the issue with the Dutch at the next meeting of the European ministers of transport..

A spokesman for the Dutch ministry of transport said it would not be making any statement until the ministry had spoken with the German ministry. - Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+44 171 542 5017
